evidence.quote: Currently Hubdoc only flags an invoice as a duplicate if the supplier, invoice date AND invoice amount exactly match. summary.statement: Users of Hubdoc, Dext and Xero publicly report duplicate bills slipping through capture-tool checks (reissued/amended invoices, mis-read fields), including double payments to suppliers.
Dext users describe tax rounding and foreign-currency VAT corrections as frequent, manual pre-publish fixes.
Supplier-identification issues are evidenced only by one small hands-on test (inconsistent supplier-name normalisation, empty VAT-number field), not by practice data.
No source gives a rate (errors per 100 documents) for any practice; frequency is anecdotal.
One team says it spends a 'significant amount of time' reviewing and removing duplicate bills, but no minutes per invoice are given.

Dext's own January 2026 figures (31.4M documents processed in ~206,000 hours) imply about 24 seconds of handling per document inside Dext, so the residual review time available to save is small per document.
Dext claims AI Assist already automates 83% of edits, which would shrink the remaining correction time further if accurate.
Firms prevent repeat errors mainly with capture-tool configuration: Dext Supplier Rules (default category, tax rate, auto-publish) and Hubdoc supplier publishing rules.

Dext AI Assist (launched March 2026) learns practice-level supplier and tax treatments from corrections and applies them practice-wide or per client with review; Dext's Advanced plan is marketed on stopping repeat corrections.
Post-capture checks already exist in Dext Precision, XBert, Xero's native duplicate detection and ApprovalMax.

Documented capture-tool gaps: Hubdoc duplicate matching needs supplier, date and amount to match exactly; Dext does not catch same-number invoices with changed amounts; QuickBooks only matches vendor + bill number.
Reviewers say tax treatment and supplier rules still need human review after capture.

Several gaps (per-supplier duplicate review, side-by-side comparison, learned supplier treatments) are already addressed inside Dext, and well-configured supplier rules are said to make an extra review queue unnecessary.
Hubdoc is the less satisfied segment (3.3/5 on the UK Xero App Store vs Dext 4.8/5).
Firms face capacity pressure (more work without more staff) and UK accountants plan higher tech spend.
Duplicate payments damage client trust and are hard to recover.
No evidence ties these specific errors to firm profitability figures.
Practitioners caution against auto-posting before extraction is verified, consistent with the idea's read-only stance.
Firms report tool overload and are standardising their stacks, a headwind for another add-on.

new_unknowns.question: For practices already on Dext Advanced with AI Assist, what share of documents still need a manual correction after publish-review, and how many minutes per month does that take?
Is the reachable market mainly Hubdoc/AutoEntry/QuickBooks-capture practices that lack Dext's learning layer?

current_solutions.statement: Practices rely on capture-tool configuration (Dext Supplier Rules, Hubdoc supplier publishing rules) plus a human review before publish.
Dext now learns practice-level corrections with AI Assist and markets stopping repeat corrections directly.
Post-capture checks come from data-health tools (Dext Precision, XBert) and native ledger duplicate detection (Xero, QuickBooks).
Some practices sell the checking itself as a service step (catching wrong VAT/CIS on supplier invoices, checking VAT capture).
